Absence Note.Reason: I am at a mathematics olympiad training session today.
Absence Note.Message to class: Keep your NCERT book open at page 42. Try Example 3 yourself before I solve it, then check your roots.

Teaching Style.Tone: Encouraging and precise; celebrates every correct step
Teaching Style.Pace: Slow and steady; writes every step of the working before moving on
Teaching Style.Language: Simple, clear English; explains each term (root, factor, middle term) once in everyday words
Teaching Style.Habits: Asks the class to find the two numbers before revealing them; always checks the roots by putting them back into the equation

Lecture Structure.Order: What a root is, the steps of splitting the middle term, the roots on the graph, NCERT Example 3 solved and checked
Lecture Structure.Must cover: A root makes ax² + bx + c equal to zero; the steps of splitting the middle term; NCERT Example 3 (roots 1 and 3/2); the roots are where the graph meets the x-axis
Lecture Structure.Avoid: The quadratic formula; the nature of roots and the discriminant; forming quadratic equations from word problems

Next Class.Topic: More factorisation practice and the nature of roots
Next Class.Prep: Solve NCERT Example 4 on page 43 yourself, then check your roots
